values: Guideline to make and understand Unit Test Case
- In the template, Unit test cases are based on functions. Each sheet presents test cases for one function.
- Cover: General information of the project and Unit Test cases

- FunctionList: The list of Classes and Functions in the document. 
     + To control that the number of Unit TC meets customer's requirement or the norm, user should fill value for  
     'Normal number of Test cases/KLOC'.

+ Click on Function link to open the related Test cases of the function.  
     Note: You should create new Function sheet before creating the link

- Test Report: provive the overview results of Functions Unit test: Test coverage, Test successful coverage 
    (Summary, for normal/abnormal/boundary cases)
Note:  Should check the formula of "Sub Total" if you add more functions

- To verify that number of Unit TC meets customer's requirement or not. User has to fill number LOC of tested function and fill value of 'Normal number test cases/KLOC' item in FunctionList sheet, which is required by customer or normal value. The number of lacked TC is shown in 'Lack of test cases' item.
- If the number of Unit TC does not meet the requirement, creator should explain the reasons.
- If the number of  'Normal number test cases/KLOC' item in FunctionList sheet is not recorded, the number in 'Lack of test cases' is not calculated.
2.2 Condition and confirmation of Test cases.
Each test case is the combination of condition and confirmation.
- Condition is combination of precondition and values of inputs.

- Precondition: it is setting condition that must exist before execution of the test case. 
                    Example: file A is precondition for the test case that needs to access file A.
- Values of inputs: it includes 3 types of values: normal, boundary and abnormal.
. Normal values are values of inputs used mainly and usually to ensure the function works.
. Boundary values are limited values that contain upper and lower values.
. Abnormal values are non-expected values. And normally it processes exception cases.

- It is combination of expected result to check output of each function. 
          If the results are the same with confirmation, the test case is passed, other case it is failed.
+ Output log messages in log file.
c. Type of test cases and result:
- Type of test case: It includes normal, boundary and abnormal test cases. User selects the type based on the type of input data.

- Test case result: the actual output results comparing with the Confirmation.
                 P for Passed and F for Failed cases.
          It can 'OK' or 'NG' (it depends on habit of the teams or customers)
- Function Code: it is ID of the function and updated automatically according to FunctionList sheet.
- Function Name: it is name  of the function and updated automatically according to FunctionList sheet.
- Executed By: Name of person who executes the unit test
- Lines of code: Number of Code line of the function.
- Test requirement: Brief description about requirements which are tested in this function, it is not mandatory.

Registers a new user account with default role 'Learner', hashes the password, and creates an associated default UserProfile.
1. Email is not already registered. 2. Default role 'Learner' exists in the database. 3. Valid input parameters.
Authenticates user credentials via email and password, updates last login timestamp, generates JWT access token, and sets refresh token in HTTP-only cookie.
1. User account exists with the provided email. 2. Account status is 'ACTIVE'. 3. Account has a password (not a Google-only account). 4. Correct password.

Authenticates user via Google ID Token. Creates a new account with 'Learner' role if not exists, or updates last login time and avatar if already registered. Returns JWT access token and sets refresh token in cookie.
1. Google Client ID is configured in system. 2. Provided Google ID Token is valid. 3. Default role 'Learner' exists. 4. If account already exists, status must be 'ACTIVE'.
Issues a new JWT access token using a valid refresh token. Implements Token Rotation by revoking the old refresh token, generating a new one, and updating the cookie.
1. Refresh token is provided via cookie or request body. 2. Token exists in DB, is not expired, and not revoked (IsActive = true). 3. User account is 'ACTIVE'.
Logs out the user by revoking the active refresh token in the database and clearing the refresh token cookie in the client response.
Retrieves basic user information (UserId, FullName, Email, Role, AvatarUrl, IsGoogleLogin) for the currently authenticated user.
1. Valid UserId extracted from authentication token. 2. User account status is 'ACTIVE'.
Retrieves detailed user profile data (Bio, Gender, DateOfBirth, ExperienceLevel, LearningGoal, PreferredLanguage) based on target UserId or currentUserId.
1. Target user exists in the database. 2. User account status is 'ACTIVE'.
Updates basic user information and detailed profile attributes. Automatically creates a new UserProfile entity if one does not already exist.
1. User exists in the database. 2. User account status is 'ACTIVE'.
Updates user avatar either by uploading an image file to Cloudinary (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp) or by assigning a direct image URL.
1. User exists and account status is 'ACTIVE'. 2. Valid image file successfully uploaded to Cloudinary OR non-empty valid avatar URL provided.
Generates a secure 32-byte reset token (15-minute expiration), saves it to the database, and sends an email containing the password reset link to the user.
1. Email is provided and non-empty. 2. Email service and ClientUrl configuration are operational.
Resets user password using a valid reset token received via email. Updates password hash and marks the token as used (IsUsed = true).
1. Token, Email, and NewPassword are not empty. 2. User exists. 3. Reset token exists, matches UserId, is not used (IsUsed = false), and is not expired.
Allows users to change their password. Requires verifying old password for standard accounts, while allowing Google users to set a password directly.
1. User is authenticated and account status is 'ACTIVE'. 2. For standard accounts: Old password is provided and matches. 3. New password is valid.
Creates a course for the authenticated instructor, validates the selected category and course data, and applies the draft or approval-submission rules.
1. Instructor is authenticated. 2. Required course fields and price are valid. 3. Selected category exists when supplied. 4. Submission prerequisites are met when requesting admin approval.
Updates an instructor-owned course, validates changes and prevents direct publishing; validates course content when submission for admin approval is requested.
1. Course exists and belongs to the authenticated instructor. 2. Update fields and selected category are valid. 3. Approval prerequisites are met when requesting admin approval.
Deletes an instructor-owned course after existence, ownership and related enrollment/payment constraints are checked according to the service policy.
1. Course exists and belongs to the authenticated instructor. 2. Deletion is permitted by enrollment and payment rules.
Retrieves the course modules in display order and maps their lesson information for the course-management view.
1. CourseId is valid. 2. Course modules and their related lesson records are available.
Creates modules and their lesson entries in bulk, applying the request defaults and mapping associated lesson video references.
1. Authenticated instructor owns the course. 2. Module and lesson inputs satisfy required validation. 3. Any referenced video-storage data is valid.
Updates the selected module fields and ordering after validating that the module exists and belongs to the instructor’s course.
1. Module exists and belongs to a course owned by the authenticated instructor. 2. Updated values are valid.
Deletes the selected module and its dependent lesson records according to the module deletion policy.
1. Module exists and belongs to a course owned by the authenticated instructor. 2. Dependent lesson data can be handled by the deletion policy.
Retrieves course lessons in the configured order and maps lesson/material details required by the management view.
1. CourseId is valid. 2. Lesson and related material records are available.
Creates lessons in bulk and coordinates the video-upload workflow: create upload sessions, upload the files to R2, and complete sessions to attach object keys.
1. Authenticated instructor owns the course. 2. Lesson data and selected video files satisfy validation. 3. Upload sessions are valid and completed for their matching lessons.
Updates lesson information and coordinates a replacement-video upload through an R2 upload session and completion step.
1. Lesson exists and belongs to the authenticated instructor’s course. 2. Updated fields are valid. 3. Replacement upload session matches the lesson and uploaded object.
Deletes lesson media through DeleteVideoAsync and then deletes the lesson record, applying the configured cleanup behavior for storage failures.
1. Lesson exists and belongs to the authenticated instructor’s course. 2. Associated media/object keys and dependent records are available to the cleanup workflow.
